dedupe_keys.name: application of heart rate variability for thermal comfort in office buildings in real life conditions

description: Fernandez, Sergio and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The completed field application tests a data-gathering and analysis procedure using wearable heart-rate sensors in an office. It examines whether physiological variation indicates stress or thermal comfort as a complement to building-management information. The reported tests show no clear comfort-versus-discomfort pattern. This negative result is retained because it bounds the proposed measurement method and its role in building-comfort modelling. The description does not identify the office location, participant count or campaign dates, so those are left unknown. It is separate from the related questionnaire/PMV field-study family; common project involvement does not prove shared observations. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
